newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The rand on Tuesday extended its losses to eight cents since last Thursday as offshore demand for dollars caught local players short and forced the currency above the 4.65 level at the close.
It was last quoted at 4.6515/6565 against the dollar from 4.6385/6435 on Monday and 4.57 at last Thursday's close.

Dealers said that initial importer demand for dollars which carried the rand to a morning's weakest level of 4.6550 was met by exporters keen to buy dollars at their best levels against the rand since October 21.

As the currency firmed to a day's best level of 4.63 bid on the dollar, dealers said the market was caught short, only to then be squeezed by London-based speculators who took the rand back up to its closing levels.
"The London guys were talking it up to the 4.65 level before New York opened and a couple of people got caught short," a dealer said.
He said that data released last Friday showing that rampant money supply and burgeoning private sector credit extension continued had been weighing on offshore sentiment.
In the short-term, dealers expected the currency to steadily weaken back towards the 4.70 level.
One said that the breach of a key technical level at 4.62 on Tuesday signalled the currency was on the road to 4.68/4.70, where the Reserve Bank was expected to offer support.
Dealers said there had been no sign of central bank support on Tuesday.
Against the crosses, the rand touched its best level in six weeks of 0.3387 against the Deutschmark as the U.S. dollar surged to a two-year high against the German currency.
It was last pegged at 0.3355/3359 marks, while against sterling it was at 7.7310/7416 from 7.8222/8353 overnight.
On the bond market, yields ended lower, helped in part by a stronger U.S. Treasury bond market.
The key R150 finished at 15.775 percent from 15.81 percent overnight, while the 30-year U.S. Treasury was quoted at a 6.34 percent yield -- its lowest since February 16.
Dealers said trade on the day had been quiet with initial local institutional and good offshore interest spurring the move lower.
But the market continued to keep a wary eye on the rand, while waiting for the release of key data later in the week.
Latest producer inflation and reserves data are due out on Thursday and Friday this week.
On the money market, all of South Africa's "big four" banks had their three-month NCD rates at 17.10 percent offered compared with a range of 17.00 to 17.10 percent on Monday.
Ninety-day Bankers Acceptances were steady in a 16.40 to 16.65 percent range.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 8.482 billion rand on Monday from 8.605 billion rand on Saturday.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of local bonds worth 49.76 million rand on Monday after buying 21.57 million rand on Friday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 3.28 billion rand from 6.17 billion rand on Friday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
